cites.quote: Three things stay the harness's job with MCP
Request i = 630 + (i − 1) × (40 + result size) tokens here.
a fluent, confident sentence is likely whether or not it's true
The model is stateless between requests: request 2 re-sends everything.
clients discover them with tools/list and invoke them with tools/call
enters the context as ordinary tokens, and the model can't reliably tell data from instructions
The cost moves from N × M integrations to N + M implementations of the same spec.
The answer was in the context window, so the model only had to rephrase it.
Harnesses trim results, return summaries instead of raw data
because turn i re-sends all i – 1 earlier results
The cost moves from N × M integrations to N + M implementations of the same spec.
the client forwards it as tools/call to the server that owns that tool
Total 2,610 input tokens for one question, not 630.
One question that needs two tools costs three requests
That is why actions that change things sit behind an approval gate
Because a tool call is generated text, it can be malformed or name a tool that doesn't exist
a claim of an action that never happened
a language ships one server and every LSP editor gets autocomplete and go-to-definition
The stop condition is a plain-text reply
Loading on demand has a price too: one extra loop turn to search before the real call.
so 10 servers × 8 tools × 150 tokens = 12,000 tokens before the user's question
Caching cuts the bill and the prefill work for the re-sent prefix, but not the window limit or the KV memory a request holds.
Cost of the definitions alone per 1,000 requests: $7.20 (each request in an agent loop counts)
